---
title: "Normal approximation of success rates"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(sigma2, sigma^2L)
hook(pi_0, subscript(pi, 0L))
task <- "llnorm1"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))

## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  pi_0 <- round(runif(1, 0.8, 0.9),2)
  N <- sample(40:100, 1)
  k <- sample((N-15):(N-2), 1)
  
  Q <- quote(search(llnorm1, llnorm1(pi_0, N, k), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())
  
  ## Quantities used in the solution text 
  mu <- N * pi_0 
  sigma2 <- N * pi_0 * (1 - pi_0) 
  sd_x <- sqrt(sigma2) 
  z <- (k - mu) / sd_x 
  prob <- 1 - pnorm(z)
  probr <- round(prob, 2)
  
  if(probr < 0.01 || probr > 0.99)
    next
  
  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(
  t$correct, t$explanations, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra
)
```

Question
========

The commonly used standard treatment for depression
has a success rate of $\pi_0=`r pi_0`$.

Using the normal approximation, calculate the probability
that at least $k=`r k`$ out of $N=`r N`$ individuals in a sample
achieve treatment success.

```{r questionlist, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========

The number of treatment successes can be approximated by the normal distribution. 
Under the normal approximation, we have $X \rightarrow N(\mu,\sigma^2)$
with expected value $\mu = N\pi_0 = `r mu`$ and variance $\sigma^2 = N\pi_0(1-\pi_0) = `r round(sigma2, 2)`$,
(standard deviation $\sigma = `r round(sd_x, 2)`$).

For at least $k$ treatment successes, we obtain $P(X \geq k) \approx 1-\Phi\left(\frac{k-\mu}{\sigma}\right).$

Using the given values, we get $z=\dfrac{k-\mu}{\sigma}=`r round(z, 2)`$. Thus, $P(X \geq `r k`) \approx `r probr`$.

```{r solutionlist, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
